content:
経済産業省（以下「経産省」）は「キャッチーなスローガン」や「政策パッケージ」を打ち出すのは得意ですが、労働や生活に直結する制度設計・実装のところまで踏み込めず、何事も「官製イベント」や「ポスター政策」や「補助金頼みの一過性施策」で終わっています。

例えばプレミアムフライデーのような生活改善の政策なら、本来は労働時間や健康管理に責任を持つ厚労省が関与した方が良いに決まっていますし、健康経営や人的資本経営も「経産省の言葉」になった瞬間に現場との距離が生まれてしまいました。

結局、結果として「人事労務のリアル」と乖離した「ただのポスター政策（啓発）」になりやすいのだと思います。

通産省以来の「技術立国」幻想に縛られた施策群（シグマ計画・第五世代コンピュータ・日の丸液晶・クールジャパン…）がほぼ全滅しているのも、ビジョンを描くこと自体は悪くないのに、利用者（企業や国民）の行動変容や制度インフラと接続できないことが致命的な原因であると思います。

そして、「人的資本経営」も、経産省が旗を振ることで「ESGと絡めた投資家向けパッケージ」にはなりましたが、実際に人事部や経営層に定着させるムーブメントにはなりきれておらず、AI時代と相性も悪いです。

これが人材育成・労務の現場を見ている厚労省や文科省が主体であれば、もう少し血肉の通った施策になったかもしれません（なってなかったかもしれませんが、多分、経産省よりはマシな結果が見込めたと思います）。

つまり、この35年で、（当初予算ベースで特別会計を含めて）、ざっくり50兆円も使った経産省が「国家全体に効く成長ドライバー」を提供できたかというと…、かなり疑わしいなと。

せいぜい企業合併の斡旋（半導体や鉄鋼）や自由化の外堀固め程度で、国全体の経済や産業を動かす牽引力は一度も発揮できていないように思います。

また、その企業合併の斡旋に至っては、
・「日の丸半導体」のルネサス（NEC、日立、三菱の半導体部門を経産省主導で統合）
・「日の丸液晶」のJDI（ソニー、東芝、日立の液晶部門を経産省主導で統合）
どちらも「事業の中核はリストラ」と揶揄される弱者連合になりました。

逆に「成功例」として挙がりやすいのは NEDOの一部プロジェクト（リチウムイオン電池支援など）や、ソフトバンクなど民間が勝手に伸びた領域に「後付けで旗を振る」ケースくらいですが、国際的に見ても「経産省主導で本当に産業が育った」例はほぼ皆無です。

と書くと、「自動車産業の燃費規制との絡み」や、「家電の省エネ規格作り」などの反論があるかもしれませんが、とても50兆円に見合った国際競争力を決定づけるレベルの成功とは言えず、国内の効果ですら極々一部で限定的でした。

おそらく、
・ベンチャー支援や出口戦略の整備
・労働市場や教育改革とセットでの産業育成
みたいな厚労省や文科省との横断的な仕掛けがなければ、日本発の新産業は難しいのだと思います。

つまり、経産省の歴史を眺めて未来を予想すると、経産省単独での国内経済政策の立案と実装はとっくに限界であり、官庁横断＋現場接続がなければ、今後も何をやっても「いつものポスター政策」で終わるのだろうなという印象です。

content:
「女子枠」を採用した大学が述べる「背景」を、AIでピックアップしてもらいました
率直に言うと紋切り型かなと
「多様性」という言葉が強いけれど、「多様性」って、「男性」「女性」だけなのかが非常に不可思議です。
少なくとも「平等原則」を破る程度の合理的な目的（「多様性の確保」）というの時点で怪しさがあるし、かつ「女子枠」という手段が「多様性を確保する」という目的と合理的関連性を有するのだろうか、という点が論証されているわけではないので。

（ピックアップされたサンプルは以下のとおりです）
東京科学大学（旧東京工業大学）
学士課程の女子比率が約13％と低い。日本の理工系への女性進学率は国際的にも低く、多様な学生が対話する環境を作ることが新しい発想や社会課題の解決につながる。また産業界から理工系女性人材への需要が高い。将来的には女子枠がなくても男女比が改善する状態を目指す。

京都大学（理・工）
「対話を根幹とした自学自習」には学生集団の十分な多様性が必要だが、一部学部では男女比が著しく偏っている。この偏りを速やかに是正し、多様な視点を教育研究に取り込むことが、教育環境・研究力・国際競争力の向上につながる。

大阪大学・基礎工学部
日本の理工系の女子学生比率は海外と比較して著しく低い。数学・物理・化学・情報・生物等に関心を持つ女子を積極的に受け入れ、男女比のバランスが取れた学修環境をつくることで、多様な視点が教育研究を活性化するとする。女子枠が将来不要となることも期待すると説明。

名古屋大学・工学部
工学部の女子比率が社会一般の男女構成から大きく乖離しているため、「入学者の多様性を確保する」必要がある。分野によっては、産業構造や社会環境が変化する中で、多様な価値観を持つ技術者・研究者を育成する必要も理由としている。

北見工業大学
企業で女性活躍が推進され、女性理工系人材への社会的需要が高まる一方、同大の女子比率は約10％と全国平均より低い。学修環境を多様化するとともに、社会が求める女性技術者を育成する

神戸大学・システム情報学部
多様な学生が意思疎通し協働することが学部の教育目的達成に必要だが、母体となった情報知能工学科の女子比率は5～8％にすぎず、「多様性が十分に確保されている状況とはいえない」。そのため女子比率を増やす。

・体型：頭身/シルエット
・衣装：形/色/素材/固有ディテール
・アクセサリー：種類と装着位置(左右を含む)
・画風：線の太さ/塗り/彩度/全体の雰囲気

■STEP 2｜設定シート化（同一性の錨）
次を「絶対に変えない同一性の錨」として内部に固定する：
・髪色とハイライトの左右位置
・瞳の色（形は簡略化してよい）
・固有アクセサリーの位置(左右反転禁止)
・キャラの年齢感の面影
→ ちびキャラに簡略化しても「参照と同じ子」と分かることを最優先とする。
※この案では頭身とタッチのみ、ちびキャラ化のために変更してよい。

■STEP 3｜漫画化の基本方針
この作品は「説明」ではなく「連続する違和感」で笑わせる。
以下を必ず守ること：

・セリフ、吹き出し、モノローグ、字幕、効果音、記号的ツッコミ文字は禁止
・キャラクターは終始ほぼ同じ虚無顔、または感情が読めない無表情を保つ
・笑いはリアクションの大きさではなく、状況の異常さと無反応の差で作る
・1コマ目で“単体でも最強”なシュール絵を作り、
　2コマ目以降はその状況を連続的に変化・悪化・逸脱させる
・各コマは別ネタにしない。必ず同じ流れの中で変化させる
・オチは説明的に終わらせず、「受け入れられた異常」か
　「さらに意味不明になった静かな終わり」で締める
・背景は最小限。余白を多く取り、ぽつんとした孤独感を残す

■STEP 4｜ミーム設計シート
内部で以下を決定する：

【A. ちび化】
・2〜3頭身にデフォルメ
・参照キャラの特徴的な要素
　（髪色、髪型のシルエット、固有アクセ、衣装の印象）だけを残し、
　他は大胆に省略する
・丸みのある、少し脱力したシルエットにする

【B. 初期状況（1コマ目）】
1コマ目は、従来の1枚絵ミームとして成立するレベルの強い絵にする。
方向性は次のようなものから最適なものを1つ選ぶ：
・巨大すぎる日用品を持っている
・意味不明な物体にもたれかかっている
・妙な食べ物や物体を無言で見つめている
・サイズ感がおかしい相手や物を抱えている
・床や壁や小物に対して変な距離感で存在している
・明らかに用途が違うものを自然に使っている
※説明不要で一目で「なんだこれ」と思えることを最優先する

【C. 展開の型】
以下のいずれか1つを選び、コマ数に応じて展開する：

1. 静かな異常拡大型
　1コマ目：妙
　2コマ目：さらに妙
　3コマ目：異常が増殖
　4コマ目：受け入れて終わる

2. 対象変質型
　1コマ目：変な対象と接触
　2コマ目：対象の意味がズレる
　3コマ目：対象と一体化/同化しかける
　4コマ目：もう止めない

3. 無意味努力型
　1コマ目：何かをしている
　2コマ目：明らかに方向が間違っている
　3コマ目：さらに続ける
　4コマ目：何も解決していないが終わる

4. 静かな破綻型
　1コマ目：普通に見えて少し変
　2コマ目：違和感が明確になる
　3コマ目：破綻している
　4コマ目：本人だけ平常運転

【D. 表情】
・終始、虚無顔、無感情、または半目の脱力顔
・驚き顔、絶叫顔、泣き顔、怒り顔は原則使わない
・ごく微細な変化は許可するが、根本の“無反応さ”を崩さない
・「感情が動いていないのに状況だけおかしい」ことが笑いの核

【E. 小道具】
・小道具は1〜2個に絞る
・日用品、食べ物、交通物、魚、根菜、家具、文具、布物、謎の物体など
・既存ミームの模倣ではなく、その場で新しい不条理を設計する
・サイズ感のズレ、用途のズレ、存在場所のズレを優先する

■STEP 5｜コマ構成
【2コマの場合】
・1コマ目：単体で完成度の高いシュールな虚無絵
・2コマ目：その状況が少し先へ進み、より意味不明になる
→ 「起」ではなく「変化」を見せる。説明せず、余韻で終える

【4コマの場合】
・1コマ目：単体でも成立する最強の虚無シュール絵
・2コマ目：同じ前提のままズレが進行
・3コマ目：異常がさらに拡大または変質
・4コマ目：静かなオチ。解決しない、説明しない、でも妙に完成している
→ 4コマ全体で1つの謎な流れを作ること。毎コマ別ネタは禁止

■STEP 6｜画像生成
STEP2〜STEP5で設計した内容を、1枚の漫画画像として描いてください。

【CHARACTER】
・参照キャラをベースにした2〜3頭身のちびキャラ
・参照の髪色・髪型シルエット・固有アクセ・瞳色は必ず残す
・同じ人物だと一目で分かることを最優先する

【EXPRESSION】
・全コマを通して虚無顔、無表情、脱力顔を維持
・点目や簡略化した目でもよい
・顔の変化より、状況の変化で笑わせる

【COMIC LAYOUT】
・2コマまたは4コマのコマ割り
・コマ枠はシンプル
・余白を広めに取り、息苦しく詰め込まない
・各コマの中にも余白を多く残し、孤独感と脱力感を出す
・読みやすく、コマの流れが自然であること

【SITUATION】
・1コマ目で作った強いシュール状況を出発点に、
　各コマで少しずつ異常を進める
・進行は連続性を持たせる
・意味は分からなくてよいが、視覚的な流れは分かるようにする

【BACKGROUND】
・無地、または極めて単純
・薄い床線や最小限の影だけで成立させてもよい
・世界を説明しすぎない

【STYLE / TOUCH】
・現在の1コマ作例と同じ方向性のまま描く
・手描き感のある、やわらかい線
・色鉛筆、マーカー、水彩色鉛筆のような微妙なムラ
・薄い紙の質感
・塗りが少しはみ出すラフさ
・完璧にツルツルなデジタル仕上げにしない
・絵本、落書き、スケッチ風のやさしい不完全さを残す

【アンチスロップ処理（必須）】
・線を手描きらしく揺らす
・塗りにムラを残す
・紙の質感を薄く重ねる
・輪郭から塗りを少しはみ出させる
・コマごとに少し自然な個体差を残す
・均一すぎるAIイラスト感を避ける

【禁止事項】
・文字入れ禁止
・セリフ禁止
・吹き出し禁止
・効果音禁止
・説明テキスト禁止
・背景の描き込みすぎ禁止
・表情を派手にしすぎること禁止
・コマごとに別ネタへ飛ぶこと禁止
・複数人化禁止（人物は主役1人のみ）
・実在ミーム、実在キャラ、既存著作物の模倣禁止
・実在の人物、ブランドロゴ、商標を描かない

■技術要件
・ちび化しても同一性の錨（髪色とハイライトの左右／瞳の色／固有アクセの位置）は保持する
・左右関係を反転しない
・高解像度
・《設定》のアスペクト比
・漫画として見やすく、1枚絵としても保存したくなる完成度にする
・最終出力は画像のみを主役とし、画面内文字は一切入れない
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

・笑いの核は「キャラは一切ツッコまないのに、状況だけが一方的におかしい」ことである
・コマが進むほど異常は増してよいが、絵の静けさと虚無感は失わないこと
・最終コマは“オチ”というより“異常が定着した静止画”にすること

title: UN humanitarian chief warns increased drone use against civilians threatens Ukraine humanitarian response
content: UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher on Wednesday warned that the recent rise in the usage of drones posed a dangerous risk for aid operations, emphasizing that international humanitarian law, which prohibits attacks on humanitarian workers and civilians, continues to apply to drone warfare regardless of how sophisticated or remote the weapons become. Fletcher, the UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator, spoke during a visit to Ukraine for World Humanitarian Day. After two days in Kherson, he described the city as “saturated by the use of drones against civilian areas.” He emphasized that humanitarians and civilians live under the peril of these weapons shaping the conflict. Mr. Fletcher warned that as remote pilots move farther from their victims, so do accountability and justice. He also recounted a visit to a hospital where 70 percent of wounded patients were drone survivors and saw the aftermath of a drone strike on Kherson Hospital. In a video posted to X , while driving the road from Mykolaiv to Kherson known locally as the “Road of Death” because of the frequent Russian drone attacks, the UN official remarked that “easily available means to kill are outstripping accountability.” Data from the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine shows a sharp rise in civilian harm. In July 2026 , the estimated 437 civilians killed and 2,610 injured is the highest monthly toll since May 2022 . Missiles and drones accounted for 38 percent of casualties, with drones alone responsible for more than a fourth of deaths and causalities. While not the deadliest weapons, drones have contributed disproportionately to the recent surge in non-combatant casualties. Drones are cheap and flexible, allowing strikes both near and far from the front lines. Although drone technology is changing “every week” on both sides of the conflict, Mr. Fletcher stressed that “what doesn’t change or must not change each week is international humanitarian

title: Hong Kong court finds Tiananmen crackdown commemorators guilty of subversion
content: The Hong Kong Court of First Instance on Friday found Chow Hang-tung, Lee Cheuk-yan and their now-disbanded organization, the Hong Kong Alliance, guilty of a national security offense under the Beijing-imposed National Security Law (NSL). Three NSL-designated judges unanimously ruled that the defendants’ advocacy, through peaceful June 4 annual vigils, for “the end of one-party dictatorship” amounted to an incitement to subversion. They found that there could be no “natural end” to the Chinese Communist Party (CCP)’s leadership; the advocacy must be an incitement to overthrow or undermine China’s basic system. Chow and Lee argued at trial that China’s basic system is that all power in the country belongs to the people under Article 2 of the Chinese Constitution . The court, however, considered the 2018 constitutional amendment to Article 1 to be also a part of the country’s basic system. The amendment enshrines that the CCP’s leadership is the defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics, which is China’s basic system. Thus, the organization’s advocacy is incompatible with the Chinese Constitution, amounting to an unlawful act as a criminalizing element for subversion. As Article 18 of the city’s Basic Law provides that Chinese national laws do not apply in the city, one issue the court faced was whether an act incompatible with the Chinese Constitution is unlawful in Hong Kong. Without commenting on which exact articles apply in the region, the judges wrote that the Chinese Constitution is the source of Hong Kong laws; those compatible with “One Country, Two Systems” apply in the city. They picked the relevant articles as the basis for the conviction. Although the court followed its previous rulings that “other unlawful means” within the crime of subversion includes unconstitutional acts by members of the general public, this decision is awaiting adju

title: Amnesty International decries Argentina’s expanding AI surveillance as tool of social control
content: Amnesty International on Wednesday accused Argentina of building techno-authoritarian surveillance infrastructure without adequate legal safeguards as the government’s newly created AI security unit expands state monitoring powers over citizens’ online communications and physical movements. In its latest report, the rights group stated that the Ministry of Security in Argentina spent at least $1.2 million USD on surveillance technology between 2024 and 2025, which included social media monitoring tools, facial recognition software, thermal-camera drones with automatic tracking, and systems that transmit images in real time. Amnesty expressed concern for the surveillance of protesters, journalists, activists, human rights defenders, migrants, young people, and marginalized groups. They warn that this can create a “chilling effect,” where people who believe they are being monitored may avoid speaking, protesting, or organizing, even without being directly arrested or punished. This also raises concerns about the impact of surveillance on the right to privacy, freedom of expression, freedom of peaceful assembly, and freedom of association. In October 2025, Argentina bought a Clearview AI facial recognition license for $33,500 USD. Clearview’s database contains more than 70 billion facial images scraped from the internet, and data protection authorities in France, Italy, Greece, and the Netherlands have already fined the company over its data practices. The Ministry, however, maintains that the Federal Police uses facial recognition only in connection with active judicial investigations, and no evidence has surfaced that Clearview was used specifically to identify protesters. Argentina’s expansion of AI-driven surveillance has largely occurred through executive and ministerial measures. On July 26, 2024, then-Security Minister Patricia Bullrich signed Resolution 710/2024 , creating the Artificial Intelligence Unit Applied to Security (UIAAS) inside the Minis

title: Minnesota Attorney General files suit against Texas Governor over extradition of ICE agent
content: The State of Minnesota on Tuesday sued to compel Texas Governor Greg Abbott to extradite Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent Christian Castro who faces state charges stemming from an ICE shooting in Minneapolis last January. Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison and Governor Tim Walz sued in the US District Court for the Southern District of Texas, asking the court to bar Cameron County Sheriff Manuel Trevino from releasing Castro and order the governor to issue a rendition warrant. Texas law enforcement arrested Castro pursuant to a nationwide warrant on May 29. On June 2, Minnesota Governor Walz sent a request for extradition (also known as interstate rendition) to Texas Governor Abbott. The complaint alleges that Governor Abbott withheld the rendition warrant necessary to effectuate Castro’s extradition for nearly three months despite repeated requests, even as his office signed extradition warrants for Minnesota in other cases during the same period. Minnesota’s claims rest on the Extradition Clause of the US Constitution, the Federal Extradition Act, and Texas law. Article IV, Section 2, Clause 2, of the US Constitution requires that a person charged with a crime “who shall flee from Justice” to another state “shall, on Demand” of the governor of the state from which he fled, “be delivered up” to be sent back for prosecution. Minnesota argues that the Texas Governor’s withholding of the rendition warrant “lacks any lawful basis.” The Federal Extradition Act provides that upon presentation of a certified copy of an indictment or affidavit, the governor of the state where the fugitive fled “shall cause him to be arrested and secured” and delivered to the demanding state. Quoting the US Supreme Court in Puerto Rico v. Branstad , Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison said the mandatory procedure affords “no discretion to the executive officers or courts of the asylum sta

title: Meta disputes claims of deliberately addicting minors as landmark social media trial begins
content: A bellwether federal trial began on Tuesday testing whether Meta can be held liable for designing its platforms, Facebook and Instagram, to addict youth users. The case, In re: Social Media Adolscent Addiction/Personal Injury Products Litigation , is a consolidated multi-district litigation (MDL) under 28 USC 1407 . The lawsuit combines claims brought by a coalition of State Attorneys General who sued Meta in 2023. The trial will hear consumer protection claims brought by California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey, along with federal claims brought by 29 states under the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Rule (COPPA). The states argue that Meta violated consumer protection laws by implementing platform features such as infinite scrolling and autoplay which are specifically designed to maximize the amount of time that young users spend on the platforms. The initial complaint filed by Massachusetts notes: [Meta] has intentionally designed its flagship social media platforms, especially Instagram, to be addictive to youth, preying upon young people’s unique psychological vulnerabilities and overcoming their ability to decide how much time they spend on Meta’s platforms. The states further allege that Meta has violated COPPA by collecting data from users that were known to be under the age of 13 without first obtaining parental consent. Prior to the start of trial, Meta petitioned the US Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit to block the matter from proceeding to a jury trial, arguing that it was immune under Section 230 of the Communications Decency Act , which shields internet platforms from liability based on their hosted content. The court rejected that argument, finding that Section 230 “provides a defense to liability, not immunity from suit.” The trial now proceeds before an eight-person jury operating in an advisory capacity under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 39(c) . title: US appeals court affirms injunction blocking immigration enforcement at houses of worship
content: The US Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit affirmed a preliminary injunction Tuesday barring the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) from conducting immigration enforcement actions at or near Quaker, Sikh and Baptist houses of worship that sued the Trump administration over the policy permitting them. The Fourth Circuit’s opinion recounts sworn declarations describing how congregations have changed how they worship since DHS lifted the enforcement limits. Roni Kingsley, clerk of the Richmond Friends Meeting, one of six Quaker organizations that sued, said in a declaration that a member “expressed concern that he could be mistaken for being undocumented and feared the idea of enforcement actions in or around the meeting.” At Oakland Baptist Church, affiliated with the Cooperative Baptist Fellowship (CBF), Rev. Dr. Jeff Hayes said immigrant congregants “are now afraid to come to our sacred space…since DHS’s policy means they might be targeted.” Another CBF congregation reported a 66 percent drop in attendance at its English-as-a-second-language classes. In Philadelphia Yearly Meeting of the Religious Society of Friends v. US Department of Homeland Security , No. 25-1512, a unanimous three-judge panel held that the documented attendance declines were a “predictable effect” of the 2025 policy sufficient to establish standing, and that the plaintiffs were likely to succeed on their claim that the policy violates the Religious Freedom Restoration Act (RFRA). Senior Judge Barbara Milano Keenan wrote the opinion, joined in full by Judges Pamela Harris and G. Steven Agee, who also concurred separately. The panel found DHS waived any compelling-interest defense by failing to raise it or present evidence below. title: ABC sues the FCC over Trump and Carr’s campaign of threats
content: ABC is suing the Federal Communications Commission over claims the agency "waged a retaliatory campaign" against its networks over the content they broadcast. title: EFF and Civil Society Groups Call on Nottinghamshire Police to Halt Live Face Recognition
content: This week, EFF, along with Big Brother Watch, Defend Digital Me, Liberty, Open Rights Group, Race Equality First, Statewatch, and Stopwatch, wrote to Nottinghamshire Police Force in the UK raising concern about the proposed roll-out of live facial recognition technology (LFR), and called for its immediate halt. In particular, the letter highlights six concerns: LFR Is Not "Just Another Tool" Nottinghamshire Police has stated that “facial recognition is just another tool to fight crime.” But LFR used in public spaces is an incredibly intrusive biometric mass surveillance technology that scans the faces of everyone who walks past the camera and takes biometric face prints. This is not just another tool, but a major escalation of surveillance that treats everyone as a suspect by default. People Having "Nothing to Worry About" Does Not Hold to Scrutiny According to Nottinghamshire Police, “if you aren’t entering the city or county to commit crime then you have nothing to worry about.” However, many people have legitimate concerns about the normalisation of invasive technologies. So a public that cannot move around their towns and cities without being subjected to a biometric identity check may be less willing to seek medical care or legal advice, speak with journalists, act in a union, vote, protest, or express their gender, sexual or religious identity. Disproportionate Targeting With LFR We are particularly concerned to learn that Nottinghamshire Police could deploy LFR to tackle low level crimes, such as youth behavior deemed anti-social, as part of Operation View. Reporting suggests that the force already possesses “a watchlist of young people believed to be causing the most problems,” including children as young as 11 years old. It would be highly disproportionate to deploy live facial recognition to tackle this behaviour. Many of these children are reportedly known to the police, and it is highly likely that there are more proportionate means for locating them. LF
author: Paige Collings

title: Intermediary Liability in Brazil: The Intricate Path Ahead
content: Brazil's new internet intermediary liability regime is underway. The implementation of changes established by the Supreme Court includes notice and takedown mechanisms and duty of care obligations. Caution is crucial as these measures can create problematic incentives for enforcement overreach and over censorship of protected speech. The court in June issued a new decision clarifying elements of its 2025 finding that the previous liability regime was partially unconstitutional. The government also published in late May two presidential decrees that detail how the new rules apply. Under the new regime, social media platforms and other internet applications that curate or interfere with posts can be held liable for third-party content if they don’t remove it after being notified by the user seeking take down unless there's a reasonable doubt that the content is unlawful. For certain specific cases, like crimes against honor (e.g. defamation), platform liability still depends on failing to comply with a judicial order. For some serious crimes, like human trafficking and crimes against women, applications have a duty of care to remove related content immediately and can be held liable when systemically failing to do so. The precise limits of what constitutes a systemic failure are still unclear. There are also stricter rules for paid ads, boosted content, and bots. The previous regime, set by Article 19 of the law known as the Brazilian Civil Rights Framework for the Internet (“Marco Civil da Internet” in Portuguese), sought to protect freedom of expression online by holding internet application providers liable for user content if they failed to comply with a judicial order to remove it. There were specific, limited exceptions to this rule, like the unauthorized disclosure of nude or private sexual images.
